title: Relative atomic mass
group: CHEM-ATOM / CHEM-PER — Atoms & the Periodic Table
examples: How do I use the abundance percentages when calculating the relative atomic mass?
If an element has two isotopes, how do I find the average mass?
What is the difference between atomic mass and relative atomic mass?

explain.say: Today we will learn about relative atomic mass.

items: Relative atomic mass is an average.
We use the abundance of each isotope.

explain.say: The relative atomic mass is found by weighting the mass of each isotope.
You multiply the mass of an isotope by its fractional abundance.
Next, you add up all these contributions to find the final relative atomic mass.
For example, if an element has two isotopes, you calculate the weighted average.
In real life, this is like calculating the average weight of a mixed bag of coins.

faq.a: Isotopes are atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons. For example, carbon-12 and carbon-14 are isotopes.
asks: How many neutrons do isotopes have?

faq.q: Why do we need to calculate the relative atomic mass?
faq.a: We use it because most elements naturally exist as a mixture of isotopes. The relative atomic mass gives the weighted average mass.
asks: Why is the average mass important?
What does relative atomic mass tell us?
Does it mean the element is mixed?

faq.a: Fractional abundance is the percentage of an isotope expressed as a decimal. You divide the percentage by one hundred.
asks: How do I change percent to a fraction?
What is the decimal form of 25 percent?

faq.q: Can I just average the masses of the isotopes?
faq.a: No, you cannot just average the masses. You must weight each mass by how much it is present in nature.
asks: Do I just add the masses together?
Why can't I just divide the masses?

faq.q: What is the difference between atomic mass and relative atomic mass?
faq.a: The relative atomic mass is a weighted average based on natural abundance. The atomic mass is the actual mass of a single, specific atom.
asks: Which one is the real mass?
Does the periodic table show either?

facts: Relative atomic mass is calculated using the weighted average of all naturally occurring isotopes.
The abundance must be converted from a percentage to a decimal fraction before calculation.
The formula involves multiplying the mass of each isotope by its fractional abundance.
The resulting relative atomic mass is a unitless number on the periodic table.

quiz.say: Element X has isotopes with masses 10 and 12. Their abundances are 75 percent and 25 percent, respectively. What is the relative atomic mass?
quiz.why: You multiply each mass by its decimal abundance and then add the results together.

wrong.0: This only adds the abundances and ignores the actual masses of the isotopes.
wrong.2: This incorrectly averages the masses without considering the abundance.
wrong.3: This incorrectly uses the first isotope's abundance for both isotopes.

quiz.say: If an element has isotopes with masses 35 and 37, and abundances of 75 percent and 25 percent, what is its relative atomic mass?
quiz.why: The weighted average is found by summing the products of mass times fractional abundance.

wrong.0: This only sums the abundances and misses the mass values entirely.
wrong.2: This is a simple average and ignores the given abundances.
wrong.3: This incorrectly assumes both isotopes have the same abundance.
